healthcareSystem: Limited public healthcare with chronic shortages of staff and equipment. Private clinics in Cotonou offer better care. Outside major cities, medical facilities are very basic. French is the medical language.
qualityNotes: Private clinics in Cotonou and Porto-Novo are adequate for basic care. Public hospitals are under-resourced. French is essential for all medical interactions. English-speaking doctors are rare. Serious conditions require evacuation.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Cotonou open 8am-7pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Duty pharmacies (pharmacie de garde) operate 24/7 on rotation.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Cotonou are reasonably stocked. Look for the green cross sign. Counterfeit drugs are a problem — avoid buying medications from street markets. French is required.
prescriptionRules: Prescriptions required for antibiotics and controlled substances, but enforcement varies. French-language prescriptions expected. Bring essential medications from home.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter in French. Keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Bring documentation from prescribing physician, ideally in French.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications, ideally translated into French. Keep all medications in original packaging. Bring generous extra supplies.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential. For serious conditions, evacuation to Accra (Ghana), Paris, or Dakar may be needed. Costs range from $30,000-100,000.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is required for all travelers. Malaria is present throughout the country — antimalarial prophylaxis is essential. Meningitis risk in the north during dry season.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink anywhere in Benin. Always use bottled or purified water. Avoid ice from unknown sources. Use bottled water for brushing teeth.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruits from street vendors. Popular dishes like pâte (cornmeal) and sauce are generally safe when freshly prepared. Be cautious with bush meat.
medicalTourismNote: Benin is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care travel to Accra (Ghana), Paris, or Dakar.
metaDescription: Health guide for Benin: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Centre National Hospitalier Universitaire (CNHU-HKM)
hospitals.notes: Main public referral hospital. Largest facility in the country. French-speaking. Can be overcrowded.

hospitals.name: Clinique Atinkanmey
hospitals.notes: Private clinic popular with expatriates. Better equipment and shorter wait times. French-speaking.

hospitals.name: Hôpital de Zone de Ouidah
hospitals.notes: District hospital near the historic voodoo capital. Basic emergency care. French-speaking.

dentalCare.availability: Limited dental care in Cotonou. Very few outside the city.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Cotonou offer basic care. French-speaking only. Equipment may be outdated.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: CNHU-HKM has a dental department. Private clinics in Cotonou may offer faster service.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Virtually none. French-speaking counselors limited even in Cotonou.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Bring all psychiatric medications from home with ample supply.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited. Most buildings lack ramps and wheelchair access. Streets and roads are uneven.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: CNHU-HKM has basic ground-floor access. Most clinics lack wheelchair accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Motorcycle taxis (zemidjans) are the main transport. Private cars can be hired.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility impairments will face significant challenges. Ganvié (lake village) and Pendjari Park are not wheelchair accessible. Plan logistics carefully.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at major hospitals in Cotonou.
covidStatus.notes: Malaria, yellow fever, meningitis, and waterborne diseases are far greater health concerns than COVID.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront cash payment (CFA francs). Facilities may not provide standardized receipts. Keep all documentation. Claims may require translation from French.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is CFA franc (XOF). Costs are low but quality is correspondingly limited.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential. Accra (Ghana) is the nearest city with adequate hospitals. Paris is common for French-speaking patients needing complex care.

drugNameMap.note: French brands dominate. Doliprane is the most recognized brand.
Available at pharmacies in major cities.
